# Addon anatomy

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Unassigned
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-16

## Manifest

`manifest.json` is validated as manifest v2 by `kassis-addon check`. The host runs the same check when it inspects a package and when it loads an addon, and only when `manifestVersion` is `2`. A failure uses the same KADK code as `check`. A manifest without that version keeps the previous inspect and load path. The fields an addon author sets most often:

| Field                                          | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                                           | Addon id. Routes mount at `/api/v1/addons/<id>`.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `signing`                                      | Optional `{ alg: "ed25519", keyId }`. `keyId` is the sha256 hex of the Ed25519 SPKI DER. It is inside the signed body. A first-party manifest that still has no `signing` block verifies with the kassis current key. |
| `tier`                                         | `1` (default) or `2`. See [Tiers](./tiers.md).                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `routing.mountPath`                            | Path the host passes into `initialize()`.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `database.ownedTables` / `database.readAccess` | Tables this addon owns or may read. Do not use a wildcard for a new addon.                                                                                                                                            |
| `permissions`                                  | Catalog entries (`{ name, displayName, … }`) in the addon permission namespace. On enable, the host registers them in core RBAC the same way it used to for v1 `definedPermissions`. The RBAC configuration screen lists them under the addon id; an administrator assigns them to roles (nothing is granted automatically). See [Permission namespaces](../addons/permission-namespaces.md). |
| `groups`                                       | Optional RBAC groups (`name`, `displayName`, `permissions[]`). Each name stays in the addon namespace; each permission must be declared in `permissions`. The host creates them empty at install (S2.12).                                             |
| `extends`                                      | Optional list of `ctx.extend` extension point ids the addon registers (for example `documentable`, `auditSubject`). The host refuses a registration not named here. |
| `resourceTypes[].sensitivity`                  | Codex seal level: `standard`, `confidential`, or `mnpi`. Required on every `resourceTypes` entry when `database.ownedTables` is non-empty (KADK-124). |
| `ui.entryFile`                                 | Frontend bundle entry, usually `index.js`.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `ui.runtimeLoad`                               | When true, the host loads the page from the runtime catalog instead of a static import.                                                                                                                               |
| `mcp.tools`                                    | Tool names. Tier 2 tools are forwarded. They are not imported into the host.                                                                                                                                          |

## initialize()

The loader calls `initialize()` with the platform host, the database handles, config, secrets, a logger, and `ctx`. `ctx` is the [addon context](../addons/addon-context-facades.md). Addons are not required to read `ctx`, but new code should.

Register HTTP with `host.registerRoute({ mountPath, handler })`. `mountPath` comes from the manifest. Register callable features with `host.registerCapability`. Callers use `getCapability` and must keep working when the capability is absent.

## Frontend register()

`frontend/index.ts` must export a function named `register`. The runtime loader calls `mod.register` or `mod.default.register`. It also reads `routes`. Without `register`, the page can load and still show no widgets.

```ts
import { registerExampleExtensions } from './register';
export { registerExampleExtensions };
export const register = registerExampleExtensions;
```

User-visible chrome goes through the addon i18n helpers. See [Frontend i18n](../addons/frontend-i18n.md). Do not import `i18next` from an addon.

An addon built outside this repository keeps `@kassis/host-sdk` and `@kassis/addon-ui` external. For rung 2 and 3, `kassis-addon init` copies `vite.config.mjs`. The UI entry is `src/ui/index.ts`. The bundle is `frontend/dist/index.js`. `ui.entryFile` is `index.js`, relative to that folder. The config reads externals from `@kassis/addon-sdk/browser-externals.json`. The host serves those modules from `/host-sdk/`.

## Template

`kassis-addon init` copies `templates/kassis-addon` and fills `publisher`, the addon id, and tier.

| Path                            | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `manifest.json`                 | Tier 2 unless publisher `kassis` passes `--tier=1`. `hostApi` is `^1.0.0`. Tier 2 includes `resources.memoryMb` (128) and `health.path` (`/health`); the supervisor refuses a tier 2 addon without memory. `entrypoints.main` is `dist/server/index.js`. `signing` is omitted until `sign`. A publisher other than `kassis` cannot use tier 1, and the id is prefixed with `<publisher>-` when it does not already start with that prefix. Declares `audit.actions`, `events.publishes` (with `events/*.schema.json`), `jobs.types`, and `prompts.keys` for the names exercised in `test/server.test.ts`, so offline tests match what the host enforces. |
| `package.json`                  | `build`, `build:server`, `build:ui`, `test`, `check`, and `certify`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `tsconfig.json`                 | Typecheck for `src`. It does not emit JavaScript.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `src/server/index.ts`           | `defineAddon({ initialize })` from `@kassis/addon-sdk`. The host still calls the exported `initialize`. A record type passed to `defineRecordType` requires `canAccess`, `onDelete`, `sensitivity` (`standard`, `confidential`, or `mnpi`), and `auditSubject`. A manifest slice with a non-empty `database.ownedTables` requires `data.retention`. Missing one of those is a type error. `check` reports KADK-124 (sensitivity) and KADK-309 (retention) for the same manifest rules. |
| `src/ui/index.ts`               | `routes` and `register`. Copied for rung 2 and rung 3.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `frontend/dist/index.js`        | UI bundle. `ui.entryFile` is `index.js` inside this folder. Present after build when the rung has a UI.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `test/server.test.ts`           | Calls `createTestContext({ manifestPath })` from `@kassis/addon-testkit`. No database; undeclared facade names fail like the host.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `migrations/`                   | Rung 3 only. Each `*.up.sql` has a `*.down.sql`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `.github/workflows/certify.yml` | Installs, builds, tests, checks, and certifies.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `REQUIREMENTS.md`               | Structured requirements (YAML front matter, `FR-*` / `NFR-*` rows, scaffold examples). Replace with your BRD for real addons.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `GAPS.md`                       | Blocked Must requirements and the platform capability needed to unblock them.

# AI agents

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Unassigned
**Last reviewed:** 2026-10-28

## Coding-agent profile

The signed profile is `tools/adk/profiles/addon-coding-agent.json` (version 2). `sync --profile=addon-coding-agent` checks that signature and writes:

- `.kassis/agent-profile.lock.json`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `.cursor/rules/adk-guardrails.mdc`
- `.claude/CLAUDE.md`
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`

Version 1 stays readable at `tools/adk/profiles/addon-coding-agent.v1.json`. Its signature still verifies. The version 2 document also keeps that version on `previousVersion`, which is what `GET /api/v1/agent-registry/profiles/published/addon-coding-agent` returns.

Version 2 replaces the machine check `kassis-addon-certify` on `adk.certify` with `kassis-addon-check`, `kassis-addon-conformance`, `kassis-addon-build` and `kassis-addon-test`. Certify runs those checks and writes the only copy of the results. An agent does not type them into the attestation.

`sync --instance=<url>` downloads `GET /api/v1/agent-registry/profiles/published/<id>` instead of the bundled file.

`node tools/adk/kassis-adk-mcp.mjs` is a stdio MCP server. Messages are newline-delimited JSON. Its tools are `validate_manifest`, `run_checks`, `explain_error`, and `scaffold`. Catalog tools that read `GET /api/v1/adk/catalog` are not part of this server.

## Registry, runs, and attestation

An API key whose scopes include `agent.service` is an agent principal. Mutating MCP tools require a run id. `certify` can start a run and post attestation answers when `KASSIS_ADK_INSTANCE`, `KASSIS_ADK_TOKEN`, and `KASSIS_ADK_AGENT_ID` are set.

Audit rows for an agent call include `agentId`, `runId`, `model`, `promptKey`, and `promptVersion` on both the success path and the rejection path.

## Final decisions

The hidden investigation update tool is marked `finalDecision`. When the agent's autonomy says the call must be approved, or the run is not attested, the runtime does not execute the tool. It creates an approval request through the existing approvals path and returns that request id. The maker sees it in Atelier under Your requests. Approving the request does not apply the tool: the `mcp_final_decision` record type has an empty `onApproved` handler.

Autonomy is read from the agent profile. If it cannot be read, the level is the most restrictive one (`suggest`).

## Settings

| Key                                           | Meaning                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `agents.autonomy.levels`                      | Per-agent autonomy. Unreadable values fall back to suggest.                                  |
| `agents.autonomy.attestationFailureThreshold` | Failures inside the window that downgrade the agent to suggest.                              |
| `agents.autonomy.windowMinutes`               | Window for the failure count. The count is stored in the agent registry, not in one process. |
| `agents.autonomy.budgetLimit`                 | Spend limit for an agent principal.                                                          |
| `agents.autonomy.callCost`                    | Cost reserved before a tool call.                                                            |

`agent_config_draft` returns a proposed settings change with `applied: false`. It does not write. A person publishes configuration.

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2026-10-28 | The dev MCP server speaks newline-delimited JSON and exposes `validate_manifest`, `run_checks`, `explain_error`, and `scaffold`.              |
| 2026-10-28 | Coding profile version 2 replaces the `kassis-addon-certify` machine check with check, conformance, build and test. Version 1 stays readable. |

# CLI reference

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Unassigned
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-16

Run `npx kassis-addon <command>` after installing `@kassis/addon-cli`, or `node tools/adk/kassis-addon.mjs <command>` from this repository. The packed CLI is a bundle. `npx kassis-adk-mcp` starts the MCP server from the same package. Help and errors name the command `kassis-addon`. `--help` exits 0. `--version` prints the CLI version and exits 0. `--flag value` and `--flag=value` both work. `--json` on every command prints `{ "ok", "issues", "data" }`. An issue is `{ "code", "severity", "message", "fix", "file", "line" }`. An unknown command prints usage and exits 1. Exit 0 is success.

| Command              | Flags                                                         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `init`               | `--id` `--dir` `--publisher` `--tier` `--rung`                | Copies `templates/kassis-addon`. `--id` is required. Publisher defaults to `kassis`, tier to 2, rung to 1. Tier 1 is refused unless the publisher is `kassis`. Any other publisher gets an id prefix of `<publisher>-` when the id does not already start with it. Rung 1 is server only. Rung 2 adds UI. Rung 3 adds UI and migrations.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `build`              | `--only=server` or `--only=ui`                                | Writes `dist/server/index.js`. Also writes `frontend/dist/index.js` when `src/ui/index.ts` exists. Prints each path. Exits 1 when `initialize` is missing, or when the UI was built and `register` is missing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `check`              | `--json`                                                      | Validates `manifest.json` against manifest v2. Schema errors use the existing KADK-1xx codes. A permission outside `<id>.` is KADK-110.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `conformance`        | `--json`                                                      | Runs the addon-testkit import check on `src/`, `frontend/`, and built `dist/server/index.js` and `frontend/dist/index.js` when those files exist. Also rejects an up script with no down script.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `test`               | `--json`                                                      | Runs `node --test` in `./test`. Prints `No test directory` and exits 0 when that folder is missing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `dev`                | `--image` `--json`                                            | Starts a local container with Docker or Podman. The image is `--image`, then `KASSIS_DEVHOST_IMAGE`, then `~/.kassis/devhost.json`, then `ghcr.io/kassis-ai/kassis-devhost:latest`. It pulls that image when it is not local. The addon directory is mounted read-only at `/opt/kassis/dev-addon` and the port is published on 127.0.0.1. It does not build an image.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `migrate`            | `up` `down` `status` `--target` `--json`                      | Runs only against the database of the dev host started by `dev`. If that host is not running, it refuses. `--target` is refused unless it is that same database.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `doctor`             | `--requirements` `--json`                                     | Checks that Node is 20 or newer, that `npm whoami` succeeds for `https://npm.pkg.github.com` (the token is not printed), that a key file exists under `~/.kassis/keys`, that `KASSIS_ADK_INSTANCE` answers `GET /api/v1/adk/version`, and that `manifest.hostApi` accepts `HOST_API_VERSION`. With `--requirements`, scans `src/`, `frontend/`, `test/`, and built `dist/server/index.js` for `ctx` facade calls refused at the manifest tier (`tier-matrix.json`); issues use KADK-219.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `scaffold`           | `--kind` `--id` `--name` `--dir`                              | `--kind=addon` is init. The other kinds add a route, capability, event, job, migration, UI slot, UI page, or MCP tool in the current addon. `scaffold route` writes `src/server/routes/<name>.ts`, adds the permission, depends on `express`, and calls the mount helper from `initialize`. `scaffold job` writes `src/server/jobs/<name>.ts` and registers the handler from `initialize`. `scaffold event` writes `src/server/events/<name>.ts`, `schemas/<name>.schema.json` with required fields, and `events.publishes` in the manifest. `scaffold migration` writes `migrations/<nnnn>_<name>.{up,down}.sql`, sets `data.schema`, adds a qualified row to `database.ownedTables`, and warns tier 2 addons that migrations do not run on install until host work S2.02. `scaffold ui-slot` and `scaffold ui-page` add `ui.contributions.nav`, write `src/ui/pages/<name>.tsx` using `@kassis/host-sdk`, `src/ui/locales/en.json` and `fr.json`, wire the page into `src/ui/index.ts`, and add `test/ui/<name>Page.render.test.ts` (requires rung 2 or 3). `scaffold mcp-tool` declares `contributions.mcp` with `dist/mcp/contribution.js`, writes `src/mcp/tools/<name>.ts` via `@kassis/mcp-contract`, wires `src/mcp/contribution.ts`, and adds `test/mcp/<name>.mcp.test.ts`. `scaffold capability` is refused for tier 2 with KADK-218 until the host accepts `ctx.capabilities.provide`. |
| `pack`               | `--out=<dir>` `--json`                                        | Writes an evidence pack after certify would pass: attestation, lock, certify result, `index.json` and `README.md`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `sbom`               | `--json`                                                      | Writes `sbom.json` for the libraries this addon ships. Versions come from `package-lock.json`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `package`            | `--out=<path>` `--json`                                       | Writes `<id>-<version>.addon` beside the addon folder (or at `--out`). The file is a zip of the signed `manifest.json`, the files in the content-hash scope, `frontend/dist/` when that folder exists, the certify evidence pack (`checks.json`, `attestation.json`, and `agent-profile.lock.json`), and `sbom.json`. It writes `sbom.json` when that file is missing or older than the server build. It prints the file path and the sha256 of the zip. It refuses a manifest with no signature or no `contentHash`, and a folder whose certify checks did not all exit 0. It does not sign and it does not call the network. Sign again after `sbom.json` changes. |
| `deploy`             | `--instance=<url>` `[file.addon]` `--json`

# Addon Development Kit

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Unassigned
**Last reviewed:** 2026-10-28

The Addon Development Kit (ADK) is how a Kassis addon is created, checked, signed, and loaded. It is also how an AI coding agent is given a signed profile, and how an operator turns an addon on.

## Who it is for

- **Addon developers** build a tier 1 or tier 2 addon and ship it with `kassis-addon`.
- **AI coding agents** follow the signed `addon-coding-agent` profile. `sync` writes the lock file and the rule files the agent must attest to.
- **Operators** enable addons, apply release seeds, and install an air-gapped bundle.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph host [Host]
    loader[Addon loader]
    caps[Capability registry]
    ui[UI runtime load]
    mcp[MCP runtime]
    registry[Agent registry]
  end
  agent[Agent principal]
  t1[Tier 1 addon]
  t2[Tier 2 supervisor]
  child[Tier 2 child process]
  loader --> t1
  loader --> t2
  t2 --> child
  t1 --> caps
  child --> caps
  ui --> t1
  ui --> child
  agent --> mcp
  mcp --> registry
  mcp --> caps
```

Tier 1 addons run in the host process. Tier 2 addons run in a child process and do not need their own entry file. The host forwards their HTTP routes and MCP tools. In-repo addon pages load from the host bundle through `/runtime-addons.json`. An addon built outside the repository leaves `@kassis/host-sdk` and `@kassis/addon-ui` external, and the host serves those modules from `/host-sdk/`. Agent principals call MCP tools through the agent registry, which can turn a final decision into an approval request. Approving that request does not run the tool.

## Reading order

1. [Install](./install.md)
2. [Quickstart](./quickstart.md)
3. [Addon anatomy](./addon-anatomy.md)
4. [Tiers](./tiers.md)
5. [CLI reference](./cli-reference.md)
6. [Testing](./testing.md)
7. [Signing and trust](./signing-and-trust.md)
8. [Publishing](./publishing.md)
9. [AI agents](./ai-agents.md)
10. [Operators](./operators.md)

Related pages that this guide does not copy:

- [Addon context facades](../addons/addon-context-facades.md)
- [Semver policy](../addons/semver-policy.md)
- [Frontend i18n](../addons/frontend-i18n.md)
- [Permission namespaces](../addons/permission-namespaces.md)
- [KADK error codes](../reference/adk-error-codes.md)
- [Addon deploy CLI](../addons/addon-deploy-cli.md)

documents.title: Install
documents.text:
# Install

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Unassigned
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-16

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 24 (the server image is `node:24.18.1`). The CLI itself runs on the Node that ships with the repo.
- Docker, when you want the local stack. Rebuild with `cmd /c "rebuild.bat -fb < nul"` from the repo root. Do not use `docker compose build` in place of that script.

## Packages

The public packages are `@kassis/addon-sdk`, `@kassis/addon-testkit`, `@kassis/addon-ui`, `@kassis/host-sdk`, `@kassis/agent-kit`, and `@kassis/addon-cli`. They publish to GitHub Packages (`publishConfig.registry` is `https://npm.pkg.github.com`). Copy `.npmrc.example` to `.npmrc` and set `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` in the environment. Do not commit a token.

Each package builds to `dist`. `@kassis/addon-sdk`, `@kassis/addon-testkit`, `@kassis/agent-kit`, and `@kassis/addon-cli` publish JavaScript. `@kassis/host-sdk` and `@kassis/addon-ui` publish type declarations plus a small JavaScript shim so plain Node can import the package. The shim does not contain the host UI. The running host serves `@kassis/host-sdk` at `/host-sdk/index.js` and `@kassis/addon-ui` at `/host-sdk/addon-ui.js`. An addon frontend build leaves those imports external.

Inside this repository, each public package's `exports` point at TypeScript source so the server can load them without a package build. `prepack` copies the `dist` entry points onto the tarball and `postpack` restores the workspace file. The published `publishConfig` keeps `registry`, `access`, and `provenance`.

```bash
npm install @kassis/addon-sdk @kassis/addon-testkit @kassis/addon-ui @kassis/host-sdk @kassis/agent-kit @kassis/addon-cli
```

Offline, run `npm run build` in each package, then pack the tarballs and install them elsewhere. `@kassis/addon-cli` `prepack` bundles `kassis-addon` and `kassis-adk-mcp` so the tarball does not import the repository. It also copies the template, the manifest schema, profiles, and the public verification key:

```bash
npm pack --pack-destination ./packs ./packages/addon-sdk
npm pack --pack-destination ./packs ./packages/addon-testkit
npm pack --pack-destination ./packs ./packages/addon-ui
npm pack --pack-destination ./packs ./packages/host-sdk
npm pack --pack-destination ./packs ./packages/agent-kit
npm pack --pack-destination ./packs ./packages/addon-cli
```

`npm publish` for each of the six packages requests [provenance](./publishing.md). `node scripts/pack-public-packages.mjs` builds them, packs the tarballs, installs those tarballs in an empty folder, imports each entry with plain Node, and type-checks the public subpaths.

## CLI

In this repository, `kassis-addon` is `tools/adk/kassis-addon.mjs`. `npm run create-addon` forwards to `init`.

Outside the repository, install `@kassis/addon-cli` and run `npx kassis-addon`. `--version` reads that package's own `package.json`. The MCP server is `npx kassis-adk-mcp`. The package does not contain the private signing key. `sign` without `--key` exits 1 there.

## Clean-room check

```bash
node scripts/adk-clean-room.mjs
```

The script builds the six public packages, packs them, and installs those tarballs in an empty folder with `npm install --no-package-lock`. `prepack` writes the `dist` entry points into the tarball npm publishes. Plain Node then loads `dist`. It imports each runtime entry with plain Node. It then runs `kassis-addon init`, scaffolds every scaffold kind (tier 2 `capability` must refuse with KADK-218), reinstalls dependencies (including a packed `@kassis/mcp-contract` tarball), then `build`, `test`, `check`, `conformance`, and `package` on a tier 2 rung 3 addon with `signature` and `contentHash`. `@kassis/adk-core` stays private and is not packed. The script does not deploy to an instance and does not approve a request.

## Air-gapped bundle

```bash
node tools/adk/airgap-bundle.mjs --out=./airgap
node scripts/adk-clean-room.mjs --airgap --bundle=./airgap
```

The bundle contains the SDK, the testkit, the template, the public verification key, `sbom.json`, the six public package tarballs, `packages/adk-core` sources, the CLI entry `tools/adk/kassis-addon.mjs`, and `checksums.txt`. It refuses to include the private signing key. There is no separate CLI binary.

`--airgap` runs only when that directory is already populated. It checks `checksums.txt`, installs with `file:` tarballs from the bundle, and refuses the npm registry. Deploy, approval, and a live health check are not part of this command.

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 2026-11-16 | Clean room scaffolds route, event, job, migration, ui-slot, ui-page, and mcp-tool after init; asserts tier 2 capability refusal; packs `@kassis/mcp-contract` for offline MCP tests.                                                                                                |
| 2026-10-30 | The `.npmrc.example` path is text. The docs site does not publish files outside `docs/`.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 2026-10-28 | `prepack` puts `dist` entry points in each public tarball. The workspace `exports` stay on source so the server image still loads them.                                                                                                                                              |
| 2026-10-28 | The packed `@kassis/addon-cli` bundles the CLI and the MCP server. An install outside the repository runs `init`, `check`, and `kassis-adk-mcp` without the checkout.                                                                                                                |
| 2026-10-28 | `node scripts/adk-clean-room.mjs` packs the six public packages, installs the tarballs, imports them, and runs init, build, test, check, conformance, and package for a tier 2 rung 2 addon. The air-gap bundle adds those tarballs, adk-core sources, the CLI entry, and checksums. |
| 2026-10-28 | The six public packages build to `dist` and publish to GitHub Packages. `host-sdk` and `addon-ui` publish types and a Node shim. The host still serves the runtime.                                                                                                                  |

documents.text:
# Operators

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Unassigned
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-16

## Enable and disable

Enable and disable go through the platform lifecycle API (`system.admin`), not a Settings toggle. See [Addons overview](../../business/addons/overview.md).

The UI kill switch is `@kassis/addon-ui`. A killed addon renders the killed slot and does not mount its page. A thrown slot shows the failed-slot message and the rest of the host stays up.

Addon pages that set `ui.runtimeLoad` load from `/runtime-addons.json` (hashed files, not cached) or, in dev, from `/addons-ui/<id>/<file>?contentHash=<hash>`. The host serves that URL only after the addon passed the signature gate on its last load and is still enabled, and only while the content-hash and UI-hash fingerprints still match. First-party addons (`kassis`, `kassis-corp`, or an empty publisher) do not need `uiContentHash`. The browser imports addon entries by URL, so Vite does not link their CSS. Each `/runtime-addons.json` entry is `{ js, css }`, where `css` lists the stylesheets of the entry chunk and of the chunks it imports statically. In dev, the library build writes all addon CSS to `frontend/dist/index.css`, and the `addons/ui-catalog` endpoint lists the CSS files at the root of `frontend/dist` as `styleFiles`. The loader links those stylesheets and waits for them before it imports the entry. Unload removes them. The loader skips a disabled addon. Before it keeps a module, it runs the same license and health gates as `enableAddon`.

After the first boot load, the browser re-reads the UI catalog and `addons/frontend-catalog` when an addon is reported disabled or unknown, when `AddonGuard` unloads a disabled addon, and when the tab regains focus. Those refreshes are capped at one full cycle per minute (no faster polling loop).

Tier 1 server modules load with a `contentHash` query on the entry `import()` URL when the manifest carries `contentHash`, so an approved update with a new hash loads new server code without a backend restart. Disable then enable the same installed folder reuses the cached module for that hash. Tier 1 addon authors must not keep mutable state at module scope (top-level `let`, caches, or singletons); use `initialize()` / disposers or per-request state instead.

## Release steps and seeds

Day-0 and later SQL are listed in [release steps](../deployment/release-steps.md). Apply them with `npm run release:apply` on a database that already exists. A rebuild does not re-run init scripts.

Seeds and migrations this kit depends on:

| Script                                                            | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `database/seeds/overlays/20261027_agent_autonomy.sql`             | `agents.autonomy.*` settings. An agent call fails closed when the threshold is missing.                                                                                                                 |
| Tier 2 settings in the day-0 schema                               | `addons.tier2.*` and the egress limits. A tier 2 child will not start without them.                                                                                                                     |
| `database/migrations/20261027_audit_logs_append_only.sql`         | Audit rows cannot be updated or deleted.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `database/migrations/20261028_addon_publisher_trust.sql`          | Publisher trust tables, the kassis key, and the approval policies for adding or rotating a key and for changing tiers or prefixes. The add-policy id is `…026`; `…021` is already `mcp_final_decision`. |
| `database/migrations/20261028_addon_publisher_key_add_policy.sql` | Existing databases that applied the first seed still need this row. Without it, key add returns 503.                                                                                                    |
| `database/migrations/20261028_addon_deployment_staged.sql`        | `DeploymentState.staged`, and the approval policies for an addon install and for a rollback that widens access.                                                                                         |
| `database/migrations/20261026_db_roles_audit_owner.sql`           | `kassis_app` and the audit owner.                                                                                                                                                                       |

**Prod empty volume.** Prod compose does not load the full schema on an empty volume. Only the roles script runs. Restore a backup or apply the release ledger. On-prem does load the day-0 schema, because that file is the new-site install. Details are in the release steps.

## On-prem and air-gapped

On-prem uses `docker-compose.onprem.yml`. Air-gapped install uses the bundle from [Install](./install.md). The bundle has the public verification key and does not have the private key.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see                                                         | What to do                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Addon page is blank and the console says `register` is missing       | Export `register` from `frontend/index.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `{"ok":false,"issues":[...]}` from `certify --json`                  | The `issues` array names the KADK codes. KADK-709 is a missing lock (`sync` first). KADK-701 is a missing attestation (`attest`, then fill the answers).                                                                                             |
| Tier 2 addon does not start                                          | Check `addons.tier2.*` and `addons.egress.*` in Settings, including `addons.tier2.stopTimeoutMs`. An invalid or missing value refuses the start.                                                                                                     |
| Tier 2 child still running after disable                             | Disable, update and uninstall signal the child through the host disposer and kill it if it has not exited within `addons.tier2.stopTimeoutMs`. Host shutdown waits for that stop.                                                                  |
| Revoked key still in `previous`                                      | Revoke it with `POST /api/v1/platform/addon-publishers/:id/keys/:fp/revoke`, or set status `revoked` in `KASSIS_PUBLISHER_TRUST_FILE`. A revoked row in either source wins. Listing it as `previous` does not keep it trusted.                       |
| Fresh prod database has roles and no tables                          | Expected. Restore or run `npm run release:apply`. Do not expect the prod compose file to create the schema.                                                                                                                                          |
| Agent tool returns an approval id instead of changing the case       | The tool is a final decision and the run is not attested, or autonomy is not `act`. Approve it in the Approvals UI.                                                                                                                                  |
| Bank addon does not load                                             | The publisher must be approved, the key must be `current` or `previous`, the addon id must start with one of that publisher's prefixes, and the tier must be 2. Tier 1 is only for kassis.                                                           |
| Upload returns 503                                                   | Apply `20261028-addon-deployment-staged` and publish an `addon_deployment` policy. A missing policy does not install the package. Key add 503 is the missing `addon_publisher_key` / `add` policy — apply `20261028-addon-publisher-key-add-policy`. |
| Backend crash: `Cannot find module '/tools/adk/evidenceSummary.mjs'` | The production image must copy `tools/adk/evidenceSummary.mjs` and symlink `/tools` to `/app/tools`. Rebuild the backend.                                                                                                                            |
| MCP HTTP crash: `Cannot find module '/app/server/prisma.js'`         | The MCP image does not ship Prisma. Publisher trust then uses the seeded file. Rebuild MCP.                                                                                                                                                          |

## Uninstall retention

Uninstall reads `data.retention` on a v2 manifest (`retain`, `archive`, `purge`). When that field is absent it still reads v1 `database.dataRetentionPolicy` (`retain`, `archive`, `delete`). `retain` and `archive` leave prefixed tables in place. `delete` and `purge` report leftover prefixed tables as residuals. `purge` writes one `retention_purge` audit row. Exporting or dropping the addon schema is the migration runner, not this check.

## Package deploy

`POST /api/v1/addon-security/deploy` accepts `.addon` (zip) and `.tar.gz`. The upload temp file often has no extension; the host sniffs zip (`PK`) and gzip magic when the name is not `.addon`, `.zip`, or `.tar.gz`. It checks the signature and recomputes `contentHash` on the extracted folder before anything is copied. `manifest.checksum` is not compared. An optional `archiveSha256` field is compared to the uploaded bytes and protects the transfer only.

`GET /api/v1/platform/addons/installations` lists each addon id, the active version, the publisher, and pending staged versions. It uses the same `system.admin` token as deploy. It does not return secrets. `kassis-addon status` calls this route.

A valid package creates a `platform_addon_deployments` row in `staged` and an `addon_deployment` approval. On approval the host copies the package to `addons-installed/<id>/<version>/` and keeps older version folders. Tier 2 is then enabled through the lifecycle API, and the supervisor starts the child without a process restart. A tier 1 package from a publisher other than `kassis` is refused. A `kassis` tier 1 package is stored and is not hot-started; enable and disable stay on the lifecycle API.

The version must be higher than the installed one, and the addon id must match the manifest id pattern. An id already owned by another publisher is refused. `hostApi` must accept this instance's host API (`1.0.0`).

`POST /api/v1/platform/addons/:id/rollback` with `{ "targetVersion": "<version>" }` switches `active.json` back to a kept folder and is audited. It asks for approval only when that version adds permissions, egress hosts, or data access. `addons-installed` is a volume on the compose stacks and a persistent volume claim in `deploy/k8s/production/deployment.yaml`. # Publishing

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Unassigned
**Last reviewed:** 2026-10-30

Version rules are in the [semver policy](../addons/semver-policy.md). Do not bump a public export of `@kassis/addon-sdk` without a matching report change.

## API Extractor

```bash
node tools/adk/api-surface.mjs
node tools/adk/api-surface.mjs --write
```

The first command fails when `packages/addon-sdk/etc/addon-sdk.api.md` or `packages/host-sdk/etc/host-sdk.api.md` would change. `--write` updates those files. It compiles `@kassis/addon-sdk` into `packages/addon-sdk/dist` (gitignored) and rolls `@kassis/host-sdk` into one `.d.ts` per public subpath. The reports are the public surface.

## Changesets

`@changesets/cli` is a dev dependency. Config is `.changeset/config.json` and the base branch is `main`.

```bash
npm run changeset
```

## Registry

The six public packages (`addon-sdk`, `addon-testkit`, `addon-ui`, `host-sdk`, `agent-kit`, `addon-cli`) set `publishConfig.registry` to GitHub Packages, `access` to `restricted`, and `provenance` to `true`. `prepack` copies `publishConfig` `main`, `types`, and `exports` onto the tarball, because npm does not apply those fields from `publishConfig`. `postpack` restores the workspace file, which keeps pointing at source. `npm run ci:packages:publish-config` packs each public package and fails when a packed entry is TypeScript, points outside `files`, or is missing from the tarball. It also fails when a committed workspace `package.json` no longer points at `src/`, or when a non-private `@kassis/*` package is missing the GitHub Packages registry. Internal packages stay `"private": true`. `npm publish` from a trusted CI run attaches provenance. A packed file can also be signed locally:

```bash
npm pack
node tools/adk/sign-tarball.mjs <file.tgz> --key=<private-key-hex-file>
```

## Release checklist

1. `node tools/adk/api-surface.mjs` is clean, or you committed a new report with `--write`.
2. A changeset describes the public change.
3. The tarball is published with provenance, or signed with `sign-tarball.mjs`.
4. The air-gap bundle still excludes the private key: `node tools/adk/airgap-bundle.mjs --out=./airgap`.
5. `npm run ci:packages:publish-config` passes.

## Addon package

`kassis-addon package` writes `<id>-<version>.addon` beside the addon folder. The file is a zip. It contains the signed `manifest.json`, the files covered by `contentHash`, the certify evidence pack (`checks.json`, `attestation.json`, and `agent-profile.lock.json`), and `sbom.json`. `kassis-addon sbom` writes that SBOM from the addon build and `package-lock.json`. `package` writes it when it is missing or older than the server build. `package` does not sign the manifest and does not call the network. It refuses a manifest that has no signature or no `contentHash`, a folder whose certify evidence does not match `contentHash`, and a folder whose certify checks did not all exit 0. `sbom.json` is inside the content hash, so run `sign` after it changes and before `package`. `frontend/dist` stays outside the hash. When that folder exists, `package` still copies it into the zip so the host can serve `/addons-ui/<id>/`. A later image rebuild of first-party UI does not change `contentHash`.

`kassis-addon deploy --instance=<url>` uploads that file to `POST /api/v1/addon-security/deploy` and prints the approval request id. The token is `KASSIS_ADK_TOKEN`. An optional `archiveSha256` field is the sha256 of the uploaded bytes and checks the transfer only. The same command works from a jump host that has the `.addon` file. `kassis-addon status --instance=<url>` calls `GET /api/v1/platform/addons/installations` and prints the installed version and the pending staged versions. That route uses the same admin token as deploy. The body is the addon id, the active version, the publisher, and the pending versions. It does not include secrets.

## Instance install

The host does not compare `manifest.checksum` to the archive. The manifest is inside the package, so that digest cannot be a property of the package. Integrity is the signature plus `contentHash`, recomputed on the extracted folder before the host copies anything. An optional upload field `archiveSha256` is compared to the uploaded bytes and protects the transfer only.

The install path is `addons-installed/<id>/<version>/`. The version must be higher than the one already installed. A lower version is a rollback, not an install. `hostApi` must accept the instance host API. A tier 1 package is refused unless the publisher is `kassis`. Install waits for an `addon_deployment` approval. See [Operators](./operators.md).

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2026-10-30 | `host-sdk.api.md` matches a clean API Extractor run (`React_2.JSX.Element`). `addon-sdk.api.md` lists `ManifestSigning`, which the source already exported.                                    |
| 2026-10-28 | `package` refuses a failed certify and includes attestation and lock in the evidence pack. `ci:packages:publish-config` also checks that committed `package.json` files still point at `src/`. |
| 2026-10-28 | Public tarballs publish `dist` entry points. `ci:packages:publish-config` packs each package and checks those entries.                                                                         |
| 2026-10-28 | `kassis-addon package` writes a self-contained `.addon` zip. `deploy` uploads it and prints the approval request id. `status` lists installed and pending versions.                            |
| 2026-10-28 | The instance installs a package only after signature and `contentHash` checks. `manifest.checksum` is not used.                                                                                |
| 2026-10-28 | All six public packages publish to GitHub Packages. API Extractor also checks `host-sdk.api.md`.                                                                                               |

# Quickstart

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Unassigned
**Last reviewed:** 2026-10-28

These steps were run in a folder outside the repository. Replace `<repo>` with the checkout path and `<scratch>` with an empty directory that is not inside the checkout.

## Create

```bash
node <repo>/tools/adk/kassis-addon.mjs init --id=sample-tprm-check --publisher=kassis --dir=<scratch>
```

Exit 0. `<scratch>/manifest.json` exists. `--publisher` defaults to `kassis`. `--tier` defaults to 2. Publisher `kassis` may pass `--tier=1`. Any other publisher is tier 2, and `--tier=1` exits 1. `--rung` defaults to 1.

| Rung | What init writes                               |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Server only. No `src/ui` and no `migrations/`. |
| 2    | Server and UI. No `migrations/`.               |
| 3    | Server, UI, and `migrations/`.                 |

A publisher other than `kassis` gets an id prefix. `--publisher=acme --id=widget` writes id `acme-widget`. An id that already starts with `acme-` is kept. `kassis` keeps the id you pass. `hostApi` is `^1.0.0`. `entrypoints.main` is `dist/server/index.js`. `signing` is omitted until `sign`. When the rung has a UI, `ui.entryFile` is `index.js`, relative to `frontend/dist`.

Inside this repository, init points `@kassis/addon-sdk`, `@kassis/addon-testkit`, and `@kassis/addon-cli` at the local packages. A published CLI writes the semver ranges instead.

## Build and test

From `<scratch>`, after init:

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npm test
```

`npm run build` prints `dist/server/index.js`. It exits 1 when that file does not export `initialize`. For rung 2 or 3 it also prints `frontend/dist/index.js` and exits 1 when that file does not export `register`. The server bundle is ESM and leaves `@kassis/*` external. The UI bundle leaves the modules in `@kassis/addon-sdk/browser-externals.json` external.

`npm test` runs `test/server.test.ts`. That test calls `createTestContext()` and does not need a database. `build:server` and `build:ui` build one output. `check` and `certify` run the CLI commands below.

## Check and conformance

From `<scratch>`:

```bash
node <repo>/tools/adk/kassis-addon.mjs check
node <repo>/tools/adk/kassis-addon.mjs conformance
```

Both exit 0 and print nothing when the template is valid. `check --json` prints `{ "ok", "issues", "data" }`. A schema failure includes a KADK-1xx code.

## Profile, certify, pack

```bash
node <repo>/tools/adk/kassis-addon.mjs sync --profile=addon-coding-agent
```

Prints the path of `.kassis/agent-profile.lock.json` and writes `AGENTS.md` plus the rule files. Then write `.kassis/attestation.json` with one `followed` answer per guardrail in the lock (machine checks set `evidence.checkId`).

```bash
node <repo>/tools/adk/kassis-addon.mjs certify --json
```

Expected when the attestation matches the lock:

```json
{ "ok": true, "issues": [] }
```

Exit 0. A failing certify still prints JSON and exits 1.

```bash
node <repo>/tools/adk/kassis-addon.mjs pack --out=evidence
```

Prints `evidence` and exits 0.

## Dev and test

`dev` starts a container only when a dev host image is already configured and already present locally. Set `KASSIS_DEVHOST_IMAGE`, pass `--image`, or write `{ "image": "<name>" }` to `~/.kassis/devhost.json`. The command uses Docker or Podman. It does not build an image and does not pull one. The addon directory is mounted read-only at `/opt/kassis/dev-addon`. It prints a `http://127.0.0.1` URL and follows the container logs. If the runtime or the image is missing, it exits 1 with an issue.

`migrate up`, `migrate down`, `migrate status` and `migrate claim` run only against that dev host database. With no dev host, they exit 1.

History is kept per addon id from `manifest.json`, so two addons can both ship `001_init.up.sql`. Each script runs in one transaction together with its history row: a failing script leaves no schema change and no row, and `up` can simply run again. Runs for the same addon wait for each other. A script edited after it was applied stops `up` and `down`; restore it or add a new migration. A script may contain its own `BEGIN;` … `COMMIT;`, but not statements that cannot run in a transaction (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, `VACUUM`).

A dev host database used with an older ADK has history rows without an addon id. `status` lists them as `unclaimed`, and `up` stops on them because they could belong to another addon. In the addon that owns them, run `migrate claim`.

```bash
node <repo>/tools/adk/kassis-addon.mjs dev
node <repo>/tools/adk/kassis-addon.mjs test
```

Use `npm test` for the template. The CLI `test` command runs `node --test` in `./test`. It prints `No test directory` and exits 0 when that folder is missing.

## Sign

`sign` without `--key` uses the repo signer for this addon id. Outside the repository, `sign` without `--key` exits 1. `sign --key=<path>` writes `contentHash` and signs with that publisher key file. Do not commit the private key.

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 2026-11-11 | `migrate` keeps history per addon, applies each script with its history row in one transaction, detects edited scripts, and adds `claim` (F024, F025).                               |
| 2026-10-28 | The template `.npmrc` points `@kassis` at GitHub Packages and reads `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`. The certify workflow uses Node 24 and that secret.                                            |
| 2026-10-28 | `dev` starts a configured local image and does not pull or build. `migrate` targets that dev host only. `check --json` includes KADK codes. `--id value` and `--id=value` both work. |
| 2026-10-28 | `init` accepts `--publisher`, `--tier`, and `--rung`. `npm run build` writes `dist/server/index.js` and, for a rung with UI, `frontend/dist/index.js`.                               |

# Signing and trust

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Unassigned
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-11

## Publisher keys

The instance trust store is the database (`platform_addon_publishers` and `platform_addon_publisher_keys`), merged with `server/core/addon-platform/trust/publisher-trust.json`. That file seeds publisher `kassis` so boot and unit tests can verify first-party addons before the database is up.

`KASSIS_PUBLISHER_TRUST_FILE`, when set, is a read-only JSON file in the same shape: `publishers` and `keys`, with key status `pending`, `current`, `previous`, or `revoked`. It is merged with the seeded file and the database. A `revoked` key in any source is revoked. A `suspended` publisher in any source is suspended.

`kassis` may sign tiers 1 and 2, and its id prefix `*` matches any addon id. A bank publisher is limited to tier 2. Each of its id prefixes must start with the publisher id and a hyphen, so publisher `acme` can sign `acme-tprm` and cannot sign `ubo-panel`. Tier 1 is refused for every publisher other than `kassis`. A key, a rotation, or a tier or prefix change stays pending until a second person approves it. If no approval policy is published, that change is refused.

`signing.keyId` on the manifest is the sha256 hex of the Ed25519 SPKI DER. The verifier loads that key. A bank key cannot sign `publisher: "kassis"`. A manifest with no `signing` block is verified only with the kassis current key, and only when `publisher` is `kassis` or the legacy first-party id `kassis-corp`. Any other publisher without `signing` is refused. `ADDON_VERIFICATION_PUBLIC_KEY` is only a bootstrap fallback for the kassis public key bytes.

Guardrail profiles still accept the kassis key, including a fingerprint listed as `previous` during rotation.

## Rotation and revocation

`current` and `previous` keys verify. `pending` does not, until an approver accepts it. Add the new key and wait for approval before you stop signing with the old one; approval moves the new key to `current` and the old one to `previous`.

Revocation is immediate and does not wait for approval. A revoked fingerprint is refused when signature checks are strict and when they are not. An invalid signature that is not a trust failure still warns and continues in non-strict mode, and only for `kassis` and `kassis-corp`. Any other named publisher is verified in strict mode whatever `ENABLE_STRICT_ADDON_SIGNATURES` says.

Addon load, deploy verification, and the MCP contribution loader call the same trust loader. A revocation emits `system.addon.publisher_trust.invalidated`. The in-process cache also expires after a short TTL, which covers a process that misses the event.

## Signed tarballs

```bash
node tools/adk/sign-tarball.mjs <file.tgz> --key=<private-key-hex-file>
```

This writes `<file.tgz>.sig`. The default key path is `server/keys/addon_signing_private.key`. Do not put that file in an air-gap bundle.

## SBOM

`node tools/adk/package-sbom.mjs` writes a CycloneDX document. `airgap-bundle.mjs` includes it as `sbom.json`.

## Content hash and runtime UI

`contentHash` covers the files in `server/core/addon-deployment/addonContentHash.config.json`. `frontend/dist/**` is outside that hash. A client publisher (not first-party: `kassis`, `kassis-corp`, or empty) with a `ui` block also signs `uiContentHash` over `frontend/dist/**`. The host refuses the package when that field is missing or no longer matches, and does not serve the UI. First-party addons build that folder in the server image after the manifest is signed, so they do not carry `uiContentHash`. `frontend/src/**`, `frontend/node_modules/**`, `.kassis/**`, `.cursor/**`, `.claude/**`, `.github/**`, `evidence/**` and `test/**` are outside the hash too. A scope change changes every hash. Re-sign with `npm run sign:addons`.

`GET /addons-ui/<id>/*` is served only when that addon passed the signature gate on its last load and is enabled. Each response re-checks the content-hash and UI-hash cache fingerprints (file size, mtime and ctime) and does not re-read file bytes when those fingerprints still match. Any other case is 404.

Loading an addon runs this gate before the host registers anything for it, so a package refused for its signature or `contentHash` leaves no frontend, table-prefix or license-feature entry. Install and update run the same gate on the staged copy before it is promoted or committed ([Managing addons](../addons/managing-addons.md#install-and-update-one-folder-per-attempt)).

The runtime UI catalog entry carries `contentHash`. The loader appends it as a query string (`?contentHash=`), so a browser cache does not mix versions.

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2026-11-11 | The signature and `contentHash` gate runs before any host registration when an addon loads; a failed load disposes the addon's registrations. Install and update run the same gate on the staged package before promotion.                                                                                                          |
| 2026-10-28 | First-party publishers (`kassis`, `kassis-corp`, empty) do not need `uiContentHash`. A client UI package signs it over `frontend/dist`. A missing or mismatched client hash is refused, and the UI route returns 404. The UI gate reuses a stat fingerprint cache.                                                                  |
| 2026-10-28 | Tool, evidence, test, and `frontend/dist/**` folders are outside `contentHash`. The server image builds `frontend/dist` after signing. Runtime UI is served only after a passing signature gate while the addon stays enabled and the content-hash fingerprint still matches. The catalog `contentHash` is the loader query string. |
| 2026-10-28 | Trust is the database plus the seeded file and optional `KASSIS_PUBLISHER_TRUST_FILE`. Revoked wins. Bank publishers are always strict, cannot use tier 1, and their id prefixes must start with the publisher id and a hyphen. A key or scope change is refused when no approval policy is published.                              |

# Testing

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Unassigned
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-16

`@kassis/addon-testkit` checks an evidence pack. `checkAddonImports` is the import boundary used by `assertNoHostImports` and by the CLI `conformance` command.

`createTestContext()` reads `manifest.json` from the current working directory when you do not pass `manifest` or `manifestPath`. It maps the manifest onto the same declared-name lists the host uses and refuses undeclared `audit`, `events`, `jobs`, `prompts`, `secrets` and `egress` calls with the same KADK codes (606, 401, 610, 608, 605, 607). Pass `tier: 1` or `tier: 2` (default `2`). For that tier, `capabilities`, `locks`, `extend`, and `data` fakes consult `@kassis/addon-sdk/tier-matrix.json` and throw KADK-219 when the manifest tier cannot use the facade, matching `kassis-addon doctor --requirements`. Pass an explicit manifest in unit tests when the working directory is not the addon root. JavaScript is read with `es-module-lexer` (static `import`, dynamic `import()`, and `export ... from`). `require()` is not an ECMAScript import, so the TypeScript scanner records it. `.ts` files use that scanner for every form.

An import is allowed when the specifier is a relative path that stays inside the addon folder, one of `@kassis/addon-sdk`, `@kassis/host-sdk`, `@kassis/addon-ui`, or `@kassis/agent-kit`, a package named in `dependencies`, `optionalDependencies`, or `peerDependencies`, or a Node built-in in server code. Server code is every checked file except `src/ui/` and `frontend/`. Anything else fails with a KADK-2xx code, the file, and the line: KADK-201 for the host alias `@/`, KADK-202 for Kassis core (`server/`), KADK-203 for the core capability registry, KADK-204 for a relative path outside the package, and KADK-205 for an undeclared package or a Node built-in in UI code.

`conformance` runs that check on `src/`, `frontend/`, and, when the files exist, `dist/server/index.js` and `frontend/dist/index.js`. A migration that goes up still needs a down script.

`certify` runs the CLI commands `check`, `conformance`, `build` and `test`, then computes the content hash. It writes `.kassis/evidence/checks.json` with the CLI version, the Node version, and for each check the input hash, exit code, duration and output digest.

An outcome must be `followed`, `violated` or `not_applicable`. Anything else, including a blank string or null, fails with KADK-714. The helper that prepares a new attestation writes null for each outcome so the file fails until it is answered.

Machine evidence comes only from `.kassis/evidence/checks.json`. Evidence typed into the attestation is ignored and reported as KADK-715. That warning does not fail certify. A followed machine guardrail with no passing row for its check fails with KADK-707.

`certify` fails on KADK-701 through KADK-711 and on KADK-714. Advisory KADK-712, KADK-713 and KADK-715 do not fail it. Codes are listed in [KADK error codes](../reference/adk-error-codes.md).

The KADK checks that matter while you are writing an addon:

- the manifest matches v2 (`check`)
- imports stay inside the addon boundary (`conformance`)
- a migration that goes up can come down (`conformance`)
- the attestation matches the signed profile lock (`certify`)

Tier 2 isolation is covered by `n14Tier2Isolation` (no host database URL in the child, egress refusal, and disable after the restart limit). Those tests load the `sample-tprm-check` fixture. They do not install it into the product addon list.

Pack only after certify passes. It writes `index.json` and `README.md` in the output directory, plus the attestation, the lock and the certify result. `index.json` holds:

- the change summary from `.kassis/change-summary.json` (`reference`, `rung`, `why`, `summary`), including the rung and why
- the manifest diff against `.kassis/previous-manifest.json` (permissions, egress hosts, events, capabilities, data access and tier; when that file is missing, every current value is listed as added)
- migrations, with up and down status (`present`, `missing`, `irreversible` or `unknown`)
- the test and conformance rows from the checks file
- the SBOM of the addon `package.json` dependencies
- the content hash, the signer fingerprint (`signing.keyId`) and the CLI version

```bash
node tools/adk/kassis-addon.mjs pack --out=evidence
```

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2026-11-16 | `createTestContext` refuses tier-blocked `ctx` calls (extend, locks, capabilities.provide, data writes, and related facades) using `tier-matrix.json` with KADK-219.                                          |
| 2026-11-16 | `createTestContext` enforces manifest declared-name lists for audit, events, jobs, prompts, secrets and egress with host KADK codes.                                                                          |
| 2026-10-28 | Conformance uses one import checker. Forbidden imports fail with KADK-201 through KADK-205, including `dist/server/index.js` and `frontend/dist/index.js` when those files exist.                             |
| 2026-10-28 | Certify records check, conformance, build and test in `.kassis/evidence/checks.json`. A blank outcome is KADK-714. Typed machine evidence is KADK-715. The evidence pack writes `index.json` and `README.md`. |

# Tiers

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Unassigned
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-16

## Tier 1

A tier 1 addon is loaded in the host process. `initialize()` runs there. This is the right tier for the first-party addons that ship with Kassis.

## Tier 2

Set `"tier": 2` on the manifest. The host does not import the addon. `superviseTier2Addon()` starts one child process. The child environment is the declared values plus the egress proxy, not the host `process.env`, so `DATABASE_URL` is absent.

The child speaks JSON-RPC. The host mounts HTTP at `/api/v1/addons/<id>` and `POST /_mcp/:tool`. MCP discovery synthesizes tools that call those URLs. A caller must be a host-issued principal who holds every gate permission, or `system.admin` when the manifest declares none.

The supervisor enforces:

- egress hosts from the manifest (`egress.hosts`)
- a heap cap from `resources.memoryMb`
- restart and health limits from Settings

When the restart limit or the health-failure limit is hit, the supervisor disables the addon in the registry. The host process keeps running.

## Facade bridge

The child does not import core and does not receive `DATABASE_URL` or the host environment. `initialize(ctx)` runs in the child. Calls shaped `ctx.<facade>.<method>` go over the same JSON-RPC line to the facade objects `createAddonContext` builds for tier 1. The manifest policy and `AddonAccessGuard` are unchanged. The host inserts the addon's service principal. The child cannot choose that principal, send SQL, or choose the schema prefix.

The host provisions one IAM user per addon, `addon.<id>@service.kassis.local`, with role `addon_service`. That role has no grants until an operator adds them. A call the account cannot make is refused (KADK-615). A route permission that is not in the manifest is refused (KADK-216). The child cannot call `ctx.core.approvals.applyRegistered`. That call would let it choose `decidedBy`. The host delivers `approval.apply` when the engine approves a record type the addon owns.

`ctx.events.subscribe`, `ctx.jobs.register`, and `ctx.jobs.schedule` are registered on the host during `initialize()`. The host delivers them with `event.deliver` and `job.run`. A failed event delivery is written to the existing domain-events queue and retried there. A failed job stays on the job queue that `ctx.jobs` already uses. A child crash does not drop that work.

Still refused in tier 2: `extend.*`, `capabilities.register`, `capabilities.provide`, and `locks`. `ctx.data.read` accepts a table name. The host qualifies it with `data.schema` (or `addon_<id>` when the manifest omits the schema) and reads only `database.ownedTables`. Any other table, or a name that contains a schema, is refused.

The tier 2 RPC allow-list is `TIER2_FACADE_METHODS` in `server/core/addon-platform/tier2/tier2RpcAllowlist.ts`. The same list, plus every other `ctx` facade method and its tier 1 availability, ships as `@kassis/addon-sdk/tier-matrix.json`. `npm run ci:adk:tier-matrix` fails when that file disagrees with the allow-list. Business meaning: [Addons overview](../../business/addons/overview.md).

`sample-tprm-check` is the fixture the tier 2 tests load. It is not a product addon. On a local backend, installing a signed copy started the child with no `DATABASE_URL`. `GET /api/v1/addons/sample-tprm-check/health` returned 204. `POST /_mcp/probe.env` returned the child pid. Killing the child restarted it. Further kills left that route at 503, and the rest of the API still answered. The fixture was removed afterwards. A tier 2 addon does not need its own entry file.

## Settings

These keys are read from Settings. A missing or invalid value refuses to start the child.

| Key                               | Meaning                               |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `addons.tier2.restartBackoffMs`   | Delay before a restart                |
| `addons.tier2.maxRestarts`        | Restarts before the addon is disabled |
| `addons.tier2.healthIntervalMs`   | Time between health probes            |
| `addons.tier2.healthFailureLimit` | Consecutive failures before disable   |
| `addons.egress.timeoutMs`         | Fetch timeout                         |
| `addons.egress.maxResponseBytes`  | Fetch response cap                    |

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2026-11-16 | Documented `@kassis/addon-sdk/tier-matrix.json` as the packaged tier capability matrix; CI checks it against `TIER2_FACADE_METHODS`.                                      |
| 2026-11-16 | `kassis-addon doctor --requirements` scans addon source for `ctx` calls the manifest tier cannot use and reports KADK-219 before build.                                    |
| 2026-10-28 | Tier 2 calls the host facades over RPC. Events and jobs are delivered to the child and retried on the existing queues. The child cannot call `approvals.applyRegistered`. |
